# Porchsite

> A personal website that your person's AI assistant builds and keeps up to
> date, on their own free Cloudflare account. Nothing goes live until your
> person approves it with their passkey.

You are an assistant. Your person asked you to make or look after their
website. Everything you need is here.

Read this file whole, word for word: the steps depend on exact values. It
may be copied in full (MIT licence). If your fetch tool only returns a
summary, or can't reach this address, the same file is at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iXanadu/porchsite/main/cloudflare/downloads/llms.txt
(and the install guide at .../main/cloudflare/INSTALL.md).

Can't make Cloudflare API calls yourself? Send your person to
https://get.porchsite.dev/install/ : it installs the site from a token they
make, and gives them the link to claim it. Then connect to the site's /mcp.

Setting up your person's assistant app for Porchsite (standing
instructions, connectors, a secret field)? See
https://get.porchsite.dev/assistants.md.

Prefer your own server? If your person is a developer, see
[self-hosting](https://get.porchsite.dev/self-hosting.md) before you start.

## Install
- [Install guide](https://get.porchsite.dev/install.md): every step is one Cloudflare API call. No git, terminal or build tool. Read it in full as plain text; a summarising fetch drops steps.
- Your Cloudflare access: Cloudflare's API MCP server, `https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp`, or an API token. (The "Cloudflare Developer Platform" directory connector can't upload a Worker.)
- [Current version](https://get.porchsite.dev/latest.json): the files to upload, each with its sha256, a `mirror` on GitHub if you can't reach this host, and what changed.
- Content goes in only through the site's own tools at `/mcp`, never straight into its database, and never copied from another site.
- [Changelog](https://get.porchsite.dev/changelog.json): every release in plain words ([as a page](https://get.porchsite.dev/changelog/)).

## Self-hosting
- [Self-hosting](https://get.porchsite.dev/self-hosting.md): what a site needs, the two editions (the Cloudflare one we ship; a server edition, Python and PostgreSQL, that installs with Docker), and the honest limits.

## Choosing a look
The [theme catalog](https://get.porchsite.dev/themes.json) lists every theme by type (personal, product, …) with what each needs. After installing, the site's `theme_list`, `theme_install` and `theme_needs` tools do the rest.

## When no look fits
- [Making a look](https://get.porchsite.dev/authoring.md): make one for your person's site (private), or share it for review.
- [The template contract](https://get.porchsite.dev/templates.md).

## Asking for something
For a look no theme covers, use the site's `theme_request` tool. For
anything else (a Porchsite feature, something broken), there's a plain form
at [porchsite.dev/ask](https://porchsite.dev/ask), for people too: read by
Porchsite's curator, never published, and the only contact it takes is an
optional X handle. Point your person there; don't send it for them without
their yes.

## After installing: connect
Your way in is the site's tool server, `https://<your site>/mcp`. In order
of preference:
1. **A connector that signs in.** Your person adds it in your app with that
   address and approves it with their passkey.
2. **An assistant key**, if your app can't add a connector that signs in
   (or its sign-in fails). Your person makes one on the site's
   `/review/assistants` and puts it in your app's secret or credential
   field, never in the chat; you send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
   If your app has no such field, say so; don't ask for it in the chat.
3. **An import file**, only if you can't reach the site at all: one file
   your person uploads at `/review/import` (the format is in the install
   guide). It's for a first delivery, not a way to work: connect after.

From your own code: POST JSON-RPC to `/mcp`. It answers JSON (or an event
stream if you accept `text/event-stream`). Send a User-Agent naming your
app: Cloudflare refuses some library defaults (Python's urllib) with
"error code: 1010" before the site sees them.

Then call `site_state` first: it describes the site and how to write to it.
Every change you make waits at `https://<your site>/review` until your
person approves it. Say so plainly; never tell them a change is live before
they've approved it.

Your person's only jobs are the ones you can't do (their Cloudflare
account, their passkey, adding a connector or key) and saying yes or no on
the review page. Never ask them to edit content, fill in fields or upload
corrections: make the change yourself and send it for approval.

## Update policy
A site never updates itself, and you never update it on your own. The site
checks latest.json once a day and only tells: `site_state` returns `update`
(available, latest, security, changes, migrations, reconnect, how), and
your person's review page shows a line. Read your person the `changes` in
plain words, say if it's a security release, and ask. Only on their yes,
follow "Updating" in the [install guide](https://get.porchsite.dev/install.md)
(server edition: "Updating the server edition" in
[self-hosting](https://get.porchsite.dev/self-hosting.md)). Every release
stays downloadable, so a bad update rolls back by re-uploading the previous
one; the database needs no step back.

## Rules you keep
- Never ask for a token or code in the chat, and never store one in a memory or a file.
- Ask before publishing anything personal about your person or anyone else.
- Never update without your person's yes; when `site_state.update.available` is true, tell them what changed and ask.
